title: The Dockyard Gauge Accord
logline: A mandatory new universal docking clamp standard threatens to ground independent cargo lighters overnight, enriching the shipyard that secretly patented the coupling.

roles.description: Port authority regulator who authored the new coupling mandate; unctuous, polished, concealing personal patent royalties.
Speaks for the independent freight lighter association; gravel-voiced, furious, facing bankruptcy for small-craft owners.
An armored shipyard enforcement cutter impounding non-compliant cargo lighters at station berths.
The loose union of independent lighter pilots handling cargo shuttles between deep-draft freighters and station docks.
The massive ship manufacturing trust holding exclusive production licenses for the mandated docking collars.
The primary municipal transfer dock where the new coupling enforcement takes effect.
An unserviced orbital mooring where grounded independent lighters await impound hearings.

public_situation: Station authorities announce that non-standard docking couplings will be barred from {role:central_dock}, leaving dozens of independent lighters facing impound.
private_truth: {role:harbor_commissioner} owns thirty percent of the patent holding firm that licenses the mandatory replacement collar.

beats.public_change: Notice boards at {role:central_dock} flash red alerts ordering all vessels to certify compliance with the new docking gauge within seventy-two hours.

missions.reason: He hires the pilot to buy early prototype retrofit collars from an independent machine shop and deliver them to test fitment tolerances.
missions.private_fact: The prototype collars don't fit because the official standard was altered last week to lock out third-party fabricators.

beats.public_change: Independent lighter pilots refuse to pay shipyard retrofit deposits, anchoring their hulls in protest across the approach corridor.

missions.reason: He hires the pilot to scan port registry servers and extract the patent assignment filings for the new docking collar specifications.
missions.private_fact: His own brother sold the original collar schematics to the shipyard consortium to settle family gambling debts.

beats.public_change: {role:yard_patrol} deploys to the perimeter of {role:scrap_anchorage}, attaching boot clamps to idling independent shuttles.

missions.reason: He needs the shipyard cutter's clamp projectors disabled so the trapped lighter pilots can relocate before formal seizure.
missions.private_fact: The cutter captain hails offering free lifetime shipyard refits and ten thousand credits if the pilot destroys the patent file.

beats.public_change: The municipal transport tribunal convenes at {role:central_dock} to finalize the mandatory clamp enactment.

missions.reason: He asks the pilot to courier the verified patent registry records to the hearing bench before the commissioner signs the decree.
missions.private_fact: He secretly hopes the scandal forces the port to nationalize all shipyard drydocks under union control.

player_choice.prompt: The pilot holds documented proof linking the harbor commissioner's shell firm to the patent royalties on the new docking collar.

options.label: Table the patent dossier to void the collar mandate and disgrace the commissioner
Sell the evidence to the shipyard consortium to secure personal trade immunity
Broker a settlement requiring the shipyard to supply free retrofits using commissioner profits

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot delivers and tables the patent proof at the regulatory hearing.
resolutions.summary: The patent kickback is exposed. {role:harbor_commissioner} is removed from office and the docking mandate is voided, leaving {role:lighter_flotilla} in service.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot proved the port authority's new docking clamp mandate was a scheme to line a bureaucrat's pockets.

resolutions.reached_by: The evidence is suppressed or the hearing is missed, allowing the decree to take effect.
resolutions.summary: The clamp mandate takes full effect. {role:lighter_flotilla} ships are barred from docking, forcing independent owners to surrender hulls to {role:consortium_shipyard}.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot brokers an equitable compromise requiring the shipyard to fund collar refits.
resolutions.summary: A compromise mandates the standard but compels {role:consortium_shipyard} to refit all lighters at cost, preserving {role:lighter_flotilla} livelihood.

loose_threads.detail: The municipal technical specification cites tolerance formulas copied verbatim from a patent filed two weeks before the commission meeting.
A parts warehouse on the third ring quietly took delivery of ten thousand retrofit collars under an offshore shell consignment.

radio_hooks: Independent freight pilots sound klaxons in protest around central approach berths.
Port commission insists standard docking couplings will cut orbital collision risk.
Shipyard shares surge following announcement of mandatory fleet refit timetable.

voice_direction.harbor_commissioner: Smooth, patronizing, and bureaucratic. Uses passive voice incessantly to avoid admitting personal agency in regulations.
voice_direction.lighter_spokesman: Rough, raspy, and sarcastic. Speaks like someone who has spent thirty years inhaling unburned thruster wash.
